Class Flow

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.Flow
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public final class Flow extends AbstractPanelElement
A run of elements laid out left to right at the panel's runtime width, wrapping onto new rows when it runs out of room: the runtime row. Holds heterogeneous children (buttons, checkboxes, labels, icons), the element analogue of SlotFlowElement. 
Flow.builder().gap(10, 4)
        .add(onOffToggle)
        .add(Flow.spacer())
        .add(resetButton)            // pinned to the right edge
        .build();

Spacers: label left, control right (§0066)

spacer() is a gap that takes whatever the row's other children and gaps leave of the Flow's width, split evenly among the row's spacers (the odd pixel to the last). A row with a spacer therefore fills the Flow's width: a label, a spacer and a control is a settings row with the control pinned to the right edge, at whatever width the panel has, with no width handed to whoever built it (a Tabs body factory never knows its width). A spacer at each end of a one-row Flow centres what is between them. When the row is too narrow and wraps, a spacer that ends up at the start or end of a row takes nothing, and the control sits under its label.

Reactive sizing

naturalWidth() is every child side by side, so the panel hands the Flow the room it has; each layout pass lays the children out to that width (a label too long for the row wraps, a button caps), wraps them into rows, and reports the hug of the result (getWidth()/getHeight(); the full width when a row has a spacer). A wrap reports its extra rows as extraLayoutHeight(), so the panel pushes what is below down.

An interactive host

The children live inside the Flow, which places them itself (in the panel's content coordinates, so they share its origin). Render and input reach them through ChildDispatch, exactly as the same elements directly on the panel: clicks, the wheel, keys, releases, popovers, attach and detach. A disabled Flow (its own disabledWhen) disables everything in it.

    • render

      public void render(RenderContext ctx)

    • renderOverlay

      public void renderOverlay(RenderContext ctx)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Second-pass render for transient overlays that draw outside the element's layout bounds (a Dropdown's popover). Runs after every element's PanelElement.render(RenderContext), so an overlay is always on top regardless of declaration order. Pairs with PanelElement.getActiveOverlayBounds(InputContext), the input side. Default: no-op.

    • getActiveOverlayBounds

      public int @Nullable [] getActiveOverlayBounds(InputContext in)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      The screen-space bounds [x, y, width, height] of this element's active overlay (an open popover), or null when none is open. The dispatcher gives an element whose overlay contains the event exclusive ownership of that click or scroll, before any hit test, and the claim rule treats the overlay as claimed whatever the panel's opacity.
      Parameters:
      in - the element's input context (its origin, so it can place the overlay)

    • notifyClickOutsideOverlay

      public void notifyClickOutsideOverlay(InputContext in)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Tells an element with transient open state (a popover) that a click landed somewhere it did not claim, so it can close. The dispatchers call it on every shown element for every click, even one another element consumed; each element decides for itself whether the click was outside. Default: no-op.

      public void onAttach(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Screen-attach lifecycle hook, called when the containing screen reaches its init(). Elements that wrap vanilla widgets register them here so vanilla's focus, keyboard and narration reach them. Default: no-op.
